question: A student is working on a project and has gathered these notes: On September 15, 1821, the leaders of the Province of Guatemala declared Central America independent from the Spanish Empire. The accompanying Declaration of Independence was composed by José Cecilio del Valle, a Honduran scholar and politician. Central America had enjoyed a degree of self-rule under the Spanish Constitution of 1812, but the Spanish king overturned that document in 1814. Valle, who had served faithfully as an advisor to the empire's administrators in the region, had long stood against independence. His outlook shifted after Colonel Rafael del Riego's 1820 uprising, which demanded the restoration of the rights taken away in 1814. The student wants to place the 1821 Declaration of Independence within the story of how Valle's political convictions changed. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
option a: It is possible that Central America's Declaration of Independence would never have been written had Colonel Riego's 1820 uprising not occurred.
option b: Valle came to write Central America's Declaration of Independence because his political outlook shifted when the Spanish king overturned the 1812 constitution.
option c: Having opposed Central American independence for years, Valle reversed his position after an uprising in 1820 and went on to write the 1821 declaration.
option d: Colonel Riego's uprising supplied the spark that Valle, a longtime opponent of Central American independence, needed in order to alter his political convictions.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Only choice C ties Valle's long-standing opposition, the 1820 revolt that changed his mind, and his authorship of the 1821 declaration together, tracing the evolution of his views.

question: By 3500 BCE the Botai, a people of the Eurasian steppe, were practicing the earliest known forms of horse husbandry, including corralling. Yet over the following centuries no trace of Botai horses appears beyond the fairly small Botai homeland: the CPONT horse strand, which dominated present-day Russia no later than 3089 BCE, shows no sign of Botai influence, and the lineage that became modern domestic horses (strand DOM2) arose from a non-Botai origin by roughly 2200 BCE. Once these horses were selectively bred for long-distance travel, DOM2 spread rapidly, dominating present-day Turkey by 2125 BCE and all of Eurasia by the close of the 2nd millennium BCE. Taken together, these findings suggest that ______
option a: the Botai probably kept horses for reasons other than long-distance travel, and their husbandry likely did not give Botai horses any obvious advantage over other horse strains.
option b: the absence of contact between Botai horses and CPONT horses is likely explained by DOM2 horses outcompeting Botai horses because of DOM2's superior long-distance travel capabilities.
option c: although the Botai probably did not go so far as to selectively breed horses to spread particular traits, they do seem to have relied on horses as a means of long-distance transportation.
option d: even though Botai horses may not have reached other regions, the Botai people's horse-husbandry techniques likely did, though not until some point between 3089 BCE and 2200 BCE.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Since Botai horses never spread and only later DOM2 horses were bred for travel, the Botai likely kept horses for other purposes and gained no clear advantage from their husbandry.

question: There are three principal categories of plant defense mechanisms: physical barriers, chemical defenses, and protein defenses. The alfalfa plant relies on a ______ the plants generate proteins that are toxic to certain plant-eating insects. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
option a: protein defense
option b: protein defense,
option c: protein defense:
option d: protein defense and
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A colon correctly introduces the independent clause that explains what the alfalfa plant's protein defense involves.

question: A student researching a topic has taken these notes: The human tongue has taste receptors for a rich, savory sensation called umami. Umami is set off by compounds present in a range of foods, among them beef and black olives. In a study, participants tasted a sample of winged kelp, a variety of brown seaweed, and rated its umami intensity as moderate. The same participants then tasted a sample of rausu-konbu, another variety of brown seaweed, and rated its umami intensity as high. The student wants to emphasize a difference between the two seaweeds. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
option a: Certain brown seaweeds, such as winged kelp and rausu-konbu, activate the umami sensation on human taste buds.
option b: Winged kelp is a variety of brown seaweed, and so is rausu-konbu.
option c: After sampling the two brown seaweeds, winged kelp and rausu-konbu, study participants judged rausu-konbu to have the stronger umami flavor of the two.
option d: Although winged kelp and rausu-konbu both possess umami flavor, umami is also present in beef and black olives.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Only choice C contrasts the two seaweeds by noting that participants rated rausu-konbu's umami as more intense than winged kelp's.

question: Across the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, Black American populations grew in numerous cities within the state of New York. During that period, many Black newspapers were established, most of them produced by and for the Black communities where they were based. The New York Recorder was published from 1953 to 1987 in New York City, New York. The Syracuse Gazette News Weekly was published from 1973 to 1976 in Syracuse, New York. Which choice most effectively uses information from the given sentences to emphasize the geographic similarities between the two newspapers?
option a: The New York Recorder was one of many Black newspapers to appear in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, launching in 1953 and followed later by the Syracuse Gazette News Weekly in 1973.
option b: A number of Black newspapers, such as the New York Recorder, founded in 1953, arose in cities across New York to give voice to their growing Black communities.
option c: From 1953 to 1987, the New York Recorder served the Black community of New York City, New York, as did the Syracuse Gazette News Weekly.
option d: The New York Recorder and the Syracuse Gazette News Weekly, both based in New York, are among the many Black newspapers that arose in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries to give voice to the growing Black communities across the state.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Only choice D stresses the shared geography by noting that both newspapers were based in New York.

question: The Dhaka Stock Exchange in Dhaka, Bangladesh, is an exchange devoted to investment in companies that operate within Bangladesh, guaranteeing that such companies are subject to certain regulatory oversight. Being aware of this can ______ prospective investors' anxieties about bureaucratic details, freeing them to concentrate instead on spotting solid business opportunities. Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
option a: assuage
option b: convey
option c: amplify
option d: designate
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Assuage' fits because the regulatory oversight eases investors' worries, letting them focus elsewhere.

question: Examining sales and price figures for 325 brands of mineral water, cooking sauces, breakfast cereals, and other consumer packaged goods, Koushyar Rajavi and colleagues found that pricing, while hardly ______ brand success, played a far smaller role in it than the breadth of retail distribution did. Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
option a: contingent on
option b: determinative of
option c: immaterial to
option d: uncharacteristic of
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Immaterial to' fits: pricing still matters to brand success even though its contribution is smaller than distribution's, so it is 'hardly immaterial.'

question: A meta-analysis of research on stemflow (rainfall that runs down a tree's trunk) went beyond noting broad areas of agreement (for instance, that tree species affects the water's chemical makeup) to ______ the narrower areas in which understanding is still thin, singling out stemflow-driven nutrient dynamics in mainly coniferous forests as one subject deserving further study. Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
option a: legitimize
option b: delineate
option c: revitalize
option d: implicate
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Delineate' fits because the meta-analysis maps out and specifies the narrow gaps in understanding.

question: Continental Divide Electric Cooperative and other member-owned rural electric cooperatives can be ______ the other principal kinds of US electrical utilities by the governance models they adopt. Public power utilities, though, like cooperatives, are not-for-profit, are owned and operated by local governments; investor-owned utilities, by contrast, are run by private boards for the benefit of shareholders. Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
option a: protected against
option b: integrated with
option c: established by
option d: distinguished from
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Distinguished from' fits because the passage separates cooperatives from other utility types by their differing governance models.

question: The passage below is from William Carlos Williams's 1925 work of creative nonfiction In the American Grain. Here Williams reflects on how American readers responded to the writings of Edgar Allan Poe, a nineteenth-century US poet and fiction writer. Poe must suffer by his originality. Invent that which is new, even if it be made of pine from your own yard, and there's none to know what you have done. It is because there's no name. This is the cause of Poe's lack of recognition. He was American. He was the astounding, inconceivable growth of his locality. As used in the text, what does the underlined figurative phrase most nearly mean?
option a: Personal experiences that are hard for others to understand
option b: Elements of the culture in which you live
option c: Inspiration you received while reading independently
option d: Ideas you have never previously expressed
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Calling Poe the 'growth of his locality' identifies him with the American surroundings and culture in which he lived.

question: Britain's North American colonies passed laws governing textiles and accessories along with the colors and designs of clothing. Although these laws had some effect on what people displayed in public, adherence to them was frequently only ______: the historical record indicates that certain prohibited items were still used and traded privately. Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
option a: theoretical
option b: clandestine
option c: superficial
option d: subversive
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Superficial' fits because compliance was only surface-level, since banned items continued to be used and exchanged in private.

question: After its heyday in the 1950s through the 1970s, Brutalist architecture—recognizable for its bulk, ungainly proportions, and exposure of raw industrial materials—fell out of fashion; it upends conventional ideas of architectural beauty. Yet whereas for decades the style's rejection of accepted taste was dismissed as off-putting, many Brutalist landmarks have lately begun attracting admirers captivated by the buildings' awe-inspiring sculptural qualities, such as the massive interlocking geometric shapes that seem to defy gravity in the John P. Robarts Library in Toronto, Canada. Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
option a: To explain how a recent rethinking of Brutalism's signature features has, in turn, prompted a reassessment of architecture's traditional aesthetic standards
option b: To defend the divisive aesthetic decisions of Brutalist architects by showing that they conform to conventional taste more closely than is usually recognized
option c: To lay out the historical reasons behind Brutalism's decline after the 1970s and its later revival in public opinion
option d: To describe how a developing shift in how the public receives Brutalist architecture reflects a change in how its aesthetic qualities are perceived
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The text's main purpose is to show how a newly emerging appreciation of Brutalism reflects a changing perception of its aesthetic qualities.

question: Text 1: With a shell measuring 1.7 meters, the extinct mollusk Parapuzosia seppenradensis is the largest ammonite in the fossil record. Ever since its fossilized remains first came to light in 1895, its size has puzzled scientists. After studying 154 ammonite fossils—including P. seppenradensis specimens from Montana and specimens of the smaller species Parapuzosia leptophylla from Austria—the paleontologist Christina Ifrim, Andrew S. Gale, and their colleagues concluded that P. seppenradensis may have descended from P. leptophylla and grown steadily larger because bigger ammonites were better able to avoid being eaten by mosasaurs. Text 2: Christina Ifrim and her team have broadened our grasp of ammonite evolution generally, but their study contains gaps that further research will need to address. For example, while there is evidence that mosasaurs preyed on ammonites, there is no direct evidence that they interacted with P. seppenradensis in particular. Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely characterize the study conducted by Ifrim, Gale, and colleagues in Text 1?
option a: It is valuable to the field overall, but part of it may lack support.
option b: It is accurate about P. seppenradensis, but its claims regarding P. leptophylla are probably exaggerated.
option c: It will likely become outdated soon, yet it draws on an impressive quantity of data.
option d: It is pertinent to the study of ammonites, but it neglects the evolutionary history of mosasaurs.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Text 2 praises the study's broad contribution while noting a gap—no direct evidence linking mosasaurs to P. seppenradensis—so it would call the work useful overall but partly unsupported.

question: The Museum of Modern Art (MoMA) in New York City displays certain video games as works of art. The 2006 game Dwarf Fortress, like other highly intricate games, is presented only through video footage, since making it playable for museum visitors would be impractical. And although this means the interactive dimension of such games is not fully conveyed, MoMA's decision to let visitors actually play simpler titles, such as 1980's Pac-Man, shows that the museum tries to convey the interactivity of games whenever it is feasible. The author of the text makes which point about MoMA's choice to include Pac-Man in the exhibition?
option a: MoMA wanted the exhibition to convey the experience of playing video games.
option b: MoMA holds that video games in general ought to be regarded as works of art.
option c: MoMA judged that most of the games in the exhibition could be represented adequately through video alone.
option d: MoMA holds that most of the games in the exhibition would be impractical to present in playable form.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Making Pac-Man playable shows MoMA wanted to convey the interactive experience of playing games when it was practical to do so.

question: By pairing dense synthesizer textures and metallic percussion with vocals electronically pitched above the natural range of lead singer Laura Les, the American duo 100 gecs typifies the contemporary electronic style called hyperpop. The style is flexible enough to take in Namasenda as well, who folds hip-hop rhythms into the hyperpop sound. Its openness has been promoted—too much so, in the view of many fans—by the streaming service Spotify, whose popular hyperpop playlist mixes central artists with clear outliers, such as the 1980s star Kate Bush. What does the text most strongly suggest about Namasenda's recordings?
option a: Their inclusion on the Spotify playlist made it possible for Kate Bush's recordings to be included as well.
option b: They indicate that she has been excessively influenced by Spotify's hyperpop playlist.
option c: They contain a stylistic element that does not appear in the recordings of 100 gecs.
option d: While some of them follow the model perfected by 100 gecs, others reject it entirely.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Namasenda's use of hip-hop rhythms is a stylistic element not attributed to 100 gecs's sound.

question: The Rarámuri language of northern Mexico has 20 vowel and consonant sounds, whereas the Hadza language of eastern Africa has 70. Why should languages vary this way? One researcher has proposed that when modern humans first appeared in Africa, they all spoke one language, but as people gradually dispersed across Africa and then across the globe, that language branched into new ones. As small groups of humans traveled still farther, those languages branched into yet more, and each new language kept fewer of the sounds present in humanity's original tongue. Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the researcher's claim?
option a: Languages that arose in Europe and Western Asia tend to have more sounds than languages that arose in Africa do.
option b: A broader variety of sounds occurs across the languages of Africa as a whole than across the languages of South America as a whole.
option c: Languages that arose in Central America tend to have fewer sounds than languages that arose in Western Europe do, and Central America lies farther from Africa than Western Europe does.
option d: The number of sounds stays fairly consistent across the various languages that arose in the last regions of Africa to be settled by humans.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: If languages farther from Africa (Europe and Western Asia) have more sounds than African ones, that contradicts the claim that sounds were lost with distance from Africa.

question: A study ranked the environmental and sociocultural benefits of urban agriculture on a scale of 1 to 25, where 1 = highest. The rankings for each of three groups—project leaders, stakeholders, and the general public—were as follows. Improvement of physical health: 5, 4, 7. Contribution to political fulfillment: 21, 23, 24. Preservation of cultural knowledge and heritage: 8, 15, 13. Prevention of soil erosion: 13, 11, 23. Enhancement of pollination: 1, 7, 12. Esther Sanyé-Mengual, Kathrin Specht, and their team surveyed three groups of people in Bologna, Italy—leaders of urban agriculture projects, stakeholders in urban agriculture (for example, food researchers and urban farming associations), and the general public—to compare their views on how much urban agriculture contributes to 25 social or ecological services the team had identified. From these ratings the researchers ranked the services for each group, with a rank of 1 meaning a group sees urban agriculture as benefiting that service the most. Relying only on the rankings in the table, a Bologna city planner promoting a new urban agriculture project concludes that advertisements directed at project leaders should highlight the project's benefit to the enhancement of pollination. Which choice best describes data in the table that support the city planner's conclusion?
option a: For project leaders, the enhancement of pollination was ranked higher than any of the other four services.
option b: The enhancement of pollination was ranked higher for project leaders than it was for stakeholders.
option c: For project leaders, the contribution to political fulfillment was ranked higher than the enhancement of pollination was.
option d: The improvement of physical health was ranked lower for project leaders than it was for the general public.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Project leaders ranked enhancement of pollination 1—higher than the other four services—supporting emphasizing that benefit in ads aimed at them.

question: When items ordered online are out of stock (OOS), retailers can ease customer frustration by offering discounts on future orders or proposing substitutions. Hypothesizing both that offering to replace an OOS grocery item (such as potato chips) with a similar item the shopper had bought before raises the rate at which substitutions are accepted, and that this increase is greater for same-flavor substitutions than for same-brand substitutions, Dong Hoang and Els Breugelmans presented two groups of consumers with different assortments of grocery products and recorded whether they rejected or accepted the proposed substitutions of each type. The researchers concluded that the first part of their hypothesis was more strongly supported than the second part. Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researchers' conclusion about their hypothesis?
option a: Although matching to past purchases lowered overall substitution rejection rates in both consumer groups, a statistically significant preference for previously purchased same-flavor substitutions over previously purchased same-brand substitutions appeared in only one of the groups.
option b: Although matching to past purchases reduced rejection rates for both same-flavor and same-brand substitutions in only one of the two consumer groups, the difference observed between the two groups was not statistically significant.
option c: Matching to past purchases produced markedly lower substitution rejection rates in both consumer groups, and its positive effect was much stronger for same-flavor substitutions than for same-brand substitutions in both groups.
option d: Matching to past purchases raised rejection rates for same-brand substitutions in one of the two consumer groups but not the other, and it had no observable effect on rejection rates for same-flavor substitutions in either group.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Choice A supports the first part (past-purchase matching lowered rejection in both groups) but only weakly the second (the flavor-over-brand advantage held in just one group).

question: Every kind of stainless steel contains differing amounts of iron, carbon, and corrosion-resistant chromium. Ferritic stainless steel, frequently used in induction cookers, however, has a greater proportion of chromium (at least 10.5%) than austenitic stainless steel does, as well as a higher iron content, which gives it its magnetic character. Austenitic stainless steel, unlike ferritic, has a face-centered cubic crystalline structure produced by adding nickel to the alloy. Austenitic stainless steel comes in two subtypes: the 200 series, often used in washing machines, and the 300 series, which contains more nickel than the 200 series and is often used in mining and chemical equipment or in compensators. Therefore, stainless steel used to manufacture ______
option a: induction cookers will have a face-centered cubic crystalline structure.
option b: compensators will have magnetic properties similar to those of stainless steel used to make induction cookers.
option c: mining and chemical equipment will contain a chromium concentration below 10.5%, whereas stainless steel used to make washing machines will not.
option d: washing machines will contain a lower percentage of chromium than stainless steel used for induction cookers will.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Washing machines use austenitic (200-series) steel, which has less chromium than the ferritic steel (at least 10.5%) used in induction cookers.

question: Publishers and printers find it difficult to produce very long books that satisfy the competing demands of readability, durability, and cost. Among some unusually long novels published in English, Victor Hugo's Les Misérables (translated from French) appeared in a 1,194-page edition and is estimated to run to 770,000 words, while John Dos Passos's U.S.A. (written originally in English) appeared in a 1,239-page edition and is estimated to run to 515,000 words. This indicates that ______
option a: the edition of Les Misérables is printed on thinner paper than the edition of U.S.A. is.
option b: the edition of U.S.A. has fewer words per page than the edition of Les Misérables does.
option c: translating a text from French into English is likely to raise its word count.
option d: page count is likely a more dependable measure of how long a book takes to read than word count is.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: U.S.A. has more pages but fewer total words than Les Misérables, so it must have fewer words per page.
